findings: Wiring an existing gate is correct surgery. Gate logic is already implemented + tested + passing on the canonical surface (78 phases, 150 IPs); slice closes the visibility gap. No new abstractions, no new kernels, no parallel coordination.
Lane is catalog-driven via lanes.yaml + ci-lanes.md mirror; quality-lanes gate enforces mirror sync. Standard wiring per the existing pattern.

findings: Gate logic already carries passing+failing fixtures in #[cfg(test)] mod. Slice does not modify behavior; no new fixture needed.
Per-PR check name `oya-foundry-fitness-master-plan-completion` is discoverable + actionable (mirrors existing fitness-* naming).

alternatives_named: Defer wiring entirely until branch-protection deployment is coordinated
rejected_reasons: Adding to branch-protection.yaml without the deployed gh-api ruleset update would cause oya-foundry-fitness-protection-context-match to fail (drift detected). Deploying the ruleset update is admin-scope (gh api PUT branch-protection) and requires user authorization. Split: this slice lands the workflow + registry rows; branch-protection deployment is F-MASTERPLAN-COMPLETION-BRANCH-PROTECTION follow-up.
Deferring entirely loses the surface-visibility gain: the lane runs locally via oya verify but doesn't post a check on PRs. Wiring it as a non-required check is still net-positive.
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Two-step wiring: visibility now (workflow + mirror), required-check enforcement after admin authorization.
